key_features: Mostly regular light-brown reticular network with fading periphery and only two brown shades, but eccentric darker hyperpigmented blotch and mild asymmetry raise some concern (likely dysplastic/Clark nevus); image-based estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Hypopigmented pink lesion with white scar-like regression areas, irregular patchy erythema, polymorphous dotted/linear vessels and faint light-brown structureless remnants, raising concern for amelanotic/regressive melanoma.

Uniform light-brown pseudonetwork with regular follicular openings, single color, fairly symmetric with fading borders, no gray dots, rhomboidal structures, or asymmetric follicular pigmentation—suggests solar lentigo/benign facial lesion.

Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, blue-gray, white, red), central blue-white veil and regression-like white structureless areas, atypical pigment network at the periphery, and surrounding erythema with dotted vessels; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Symmetric, well-circumscribed light-to-medium brown lesion with uniform peripheral rim of globules and homogeneous center, no atypical network, streaks, or blue-white veil — consistent with a growing benign (Clark/compound) nevus; image-based estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Small lesion with globular pattern, peripheral brown globules fairly regularly distributed, central darker brown-gray homogeneous area, no atypical network, streaks, or blue-white veil; mild asymmetry suggests a growing/dysplastic nevus.

Asymmetric, ill-defined irregular brown pigmentation on sun-damaged skin with central regression-like white/pink areas, focal gray-blue granularity, and asymmetric perifollicular pigmentation suggestive of lentigo maligna-type melanoma; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Pink cobblestone/papillomatous lobules with comma-like vessels and small brown keratin-filled clefts, no pigment network or atypical melanocytic structures, consistent with a papillomatous dermal nevus or similar benign lesion.

Large asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged skin with central regression (white scar-like and pink areas with gray-blue granularity/peppering), irregularly distributed brown dots and granules, and ill-defined patchy pigmentation, suggestive of lentigo maligna/regressing melanoma.

Light-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with moth-eaten, sharply demarcated borders, fine reticular/fingerprint-like pattern and milia-like openings suggesting solar lentigo/flat seborrheic keratosis; mild asymmetry and central greyish structureless area with some dots raise modest concern for lentigo maligna.

Well-circumscribed central yellow-orange serous crust/erosion on pink erythematous scaly background with no pigment network, globules, streaks, or blue-white structures; pattern favors non-melanocytic lesion (e.g., keratinocytic lesion such as Bowen's/SCC/BCC or inflammatory erosion), though amelanotic melanoma cannot be fully excluded.
Asymmetric multicolored lesion with prominent blue-white veil, regression-like white/pink scar-like areas, dotted vessels, irregular brown-black peripheral pigmentation and blotches.

Asymmetric lesion with large central scar-like white/pink regression areas, blue-gray peppering (granularity), atypical broken pigment network at the periphery, and irregular borders; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular, ill-defined borders, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, blue-gray, pinkish areas), eccentric dark hyperpigmented blotch, and regression-like gray/white structureless zones.

Asymmetric, ill-defined lesion on sun-damaged skin with irregular light-to-dark brown pigmentation, atypical pseudonetwork/perifollicular pigmentation, white scar-like regression areas and prominent irregular vessels, suggesting lentigo maligna-type melanoma.

Large asymmetric lesion with irregular scalloped borders, multiple colors (light/dark brown, black, blue-gray, pink), eccentric dark blotch, and pink-white regression-like structureless areas with vascular erythema.

Small, faint light-brown pigment remnant centered in a white scar-like/regression area on sun-damaged pink skin with scale, no atypical network, streaks, blue-gray structures or polymorphous vessels; favors benign keratosis/regressing lentigo, though regression warrants some caution.

Large asymmetric lesion with ill-defined pinkish-erythematous background, irregular patchy light-to-dark brown pigmentation, focal white scar-like/regression areas, and polymorphous dotted/linear vessels suggesting a hypomelanotic melanoma.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular jagged borders, multiple colors (light/dark brown, pink-red, blue-gray foci), central pink/white regression-like structureless areas, irregular peripheral dots/globules, on sun-damaged skin.

Pink-red ill-defined patch with regularly distributed dotted vessels, faint light-brown structureless areas, and no pigment network or melanoma-specific structures, favoring an inflammatory or keratinocytic lesion (e.g., lichenoid keratosis/Bowen-type) though amelanotic melanoma cannot be fully excluded.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light/dark brown, blue-gray, white, pink-red), extensive white scar-like regression areas, blue-white veil, and irregular peripheral pigment blotches.

Small lesion with light-to-dark brown pigmentation, central darker area with globules/dots and somewhat irregular peripheral dots and border, but limited colors, no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels; background sun-damaged skin—favors a nevus (possibly dysplastic), image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Large (>10 mm) asymmetric, ill-defined light-to-dark brown patch on sun-damaged skin with irregular patchy pigmentation, focal blue-gray/dark dots centrally, and whitish regression-like areas, suggestive of lentigo maligna-type melanoma.

Large (>15 mm) asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, extensive central regression-like scar-like pink-white areas with dotted vessels, gray peppering centrally, and uneven peripheral light-brown pigment network with focal darker eccentric area.

Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown, black, blue-gray), blue-white veil-like structureless areas, irregular peripheral dots/globules and blotches, and ill-defined irregular borders; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Large asymmetric lesion with atypical/broken pigment network, extensive white scar-like regression areas, gray granularity (peppering), and pinkish vascular areas suggest regressing superficial spreading melanoma; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.
Large asymmetric lesion with prominent blue-gray/blue-white veil, regression-like whitish areas, irregular brown dots/globules, multiple colors and ill-defined irregular border.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (dark brown, black, blue-gray, light tan), irregular dark blotches/granularity and eccentric hyperpigmentation on sun-damaged skin, suggestive of melanoma (lentigo maligna type); image-based estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Predominantly globular/cobblestone pattern with brown globules fairly regularly distributed and light-brown background, though mild asymmetry, an eccentric darker purplish-brown center, a satellite tan patch and focal pink areas add some atypia, favoring a dysplastic/compound nevus over melanoma.

Large scar-like white regression area with pink erythema, irregular linear/dotted vessels, and eccentric residual dark brown-black irregular pigment blotches and granules at the periphery, suggesting extensively regressed melanoma.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown macule with a faint reticular/fibrillar pattern, mild two-tone color (olive-brown and reddish-brown) with a central pinkish area, no blue-white veil, atypical streaks, or irregular dots/globules; background sun-damaged skin with lentigines favors a benign nevus/solar lentigo, though mild color asymmetry raises some concern.

Asymmetric lesion with central scar-like white-pink regression area, irregular peripheral brown pigment network, multiple colors (light/dark brown, pink, white, focal dark blotch), and irregular borders on sun-damaged skin; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Large asymmetric lesion with extensive white scar-like regression areas, pink-red milky areas with dotted/irregular vessels, focal blue-gray peppering, and residual irregular eccentric brown pigmentation suggest regressing melanoma; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Large asymmetric lesion with ill-defined irregular borders, multifocal patchy hyperpigmentation, atypical/broken pigment network with varying shades of brown, and central hypopigmented regression-like areas; educational estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Large (~9 mm) asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light/dark brown, blue-gray, pink), blue-white veil and regression-like areas, atypical network and irregular dots/globules on sun-damaged skin.

Light-brown, moth-eaten, patchy pigmentation with faint reticular/fingerprint-like pattern on sun-damaged skin with multiple similar surrounding lentigines, suggesting solar lentigo/lichenoid keratosis; focal eccentric dark crusted area and irregular outline raise some concern for lentigo maligna-type melanoma.

Large asymmetric lesion with irregular jagged borders, atypical broken pigment network, eccentric dark brown blotches, multifocal hypopigmented/regression-like areas, and a scaly crusted zone—suggestive of superficial spreading melanoma/lentigo maligna pattern; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Large pink-red hypopigmented nodule with polymorphous atypical vessels (serpentine, coiled, irregular linear), milky-red areas, and adjacent blue-gray/brown irregular pigmentation with white regression-like areas, suggesting amelanotic/hypomelanotic nodular melanoma.

Small but asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, blue-gray/violaceous center), irregular peripheral dots/granules, and surrounding pink erythema on sun-damaged skin.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular jagged borders, atypical broadened pigment network, multiple shades of brown with eccentric dark blotches and focal hypopigmented regression-like areas.

Sun-damaged facial skin with prominent telangiectasia showing asymmetric perifollicular brown-gray pigmentation, annular-granular pattern, rhomboidal/angulated lines and focal blue-gray to dark blotches suggestive of lentigo maligna.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light/dark brown, gray, pink), central whitish-pink regression-like scar area with irregular dotted/linear vessels, and eccentric dark structureless blotches at the periphery.

Asymmetric, ill-defined irregular brown-gray pigmentation with central whitish-blue regression-like area on sun-damaged skin with prominent telangiectatic vessels, lacking a benign organized pattern; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Asymmetric, irregularly bordered light-to-dark brown pigmentation with gray granular dots (regression/peppering), whitish scar-like regression areas, and erythematous sun-damaged background with vessels, suggestive of lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Asymmetric ill-defined lesion on sun-damaged skin with multiple colors (light/dark brown, pink-red, blue-gray areas), regression-like whitish zones, erythema and atypical pigment pattern suggestive of melanoma in situ/early invasive melanoma.

Large asymmetric lesion with extensive central white-pink scar-like regression area, irregular peripheral pigmented blotches, atypical network remnants, gray-blue areas and subtle vessels, suggestive of regressing melanoma; image-based estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, blue-gray, pink), central blue-gray veil/regression-like areas, irregular dots/globules and atypical peripheral network on sun-damaged skin.

Small (~2 mm) focal brown-gray pigmented spot adjacent to an ill-defined pink-red erythematous area with fine vessels on sun-damaged skin; no clear network, streaks, or multi-color atypia, though eccentric pigment with erythema/regression-like background leaves some concern; image-based estimate only, not a diagnosis.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, black, blue-gray/white veil-like areas), atypical irregular network with peripheral streaks/pseudopods, irregular blotches and crusted/ulcerated dark region.

Small lesion with fairly uniform brown globular/cobblestone pattern and peripheral globules, limited colors (light to dark brown), mild asymmetry of shape and slightly darker eccentric center but no blue-white veil, atypical network, or streaks; favors a globular (possibly growing/dysplastic) nevus.

Asymmetric lesion with eccentric light-brown structureless pigmentation adjacent to a pink-white regression-like area with radially arranged dotted/linear irregular vessels and milky-red zones, suggesting a hypomelanotic melanoma with regression; this is a research estimate, not a clinical diagnosis.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular fading borders, multiple shades of brown, central whitish-pink regression-like/scaly area with bluish-gray structures and eccentric dark blotches/irregular globules.

Asymmetric, ill-defined lesion with irregular light-to-dark brown and gray pigmentation, whitish regression-like structureless areas, pink erythema with irregular linear vessels, and absence of an organized benign pattern; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Small, light-to-medium brown lesion with a fairly regular pigment network fading at the periphery, though slightly irregular outline, a few blue-gray dots and small hypopigmented structureless areas add mild atypia; image-based research estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Small, fairly symmetric lesion with a regular reticular pigment network, central hyperpigmentation fading gradually at the periphery, uniform brown color and no blue-white veil, atypical streaks or regression structures; image-based estimate only, not a clinical diagnosis.

Small light-to-medium brown lesion with fairly regular reticular/globular pigment pattern and single color family, but eccentric pink structureless area with asymmetry on one side raises some concern for regression or early melanoma.

Light to medium brown lesion with faint regular reticular/structureless pattern, two-tone asymmetry but no blue-white veil, atypical network, streaks, irregular dots or regression; background of solar lentigines suggests benign nevus/lentigo, though asymmetry warrants some concern.

Asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged skin with white scar-like regression areas, blue-gray irregular pigmentation/peppering, pink-red vascular erythema, shiny white streaks, and irregular brown peripheral pigmentation suggestive of regressing melanoma (lentigo maligna type).

Faint light-brown/yellowish patchy pigmentation with ill-defined borders on sun-damaged skin, no dark network, blue-gray structures, or atypical vessels; favors solar lentigo/pigmented actinic keratosis, though lentigo maligna cannot be fully excluded.

Light brown, patchy, ill-defined pigmentation with faint reticular/pseudonetwork pattern on sun-damaged skin, uniform tan color without dark, blue-gray, or atypical structures; favors solar lentigo, though lentigo maligna cannot be excluded.

Asymmetric irregularly bordered brown patch on severely sun-damaged skin with variegated light-to-dark brown pigment, focal blue-gray areas suggesting regression, and reddish zones, suggestive of lentigo maligna-type melanoma; image-based estimate only, not a diagnosis.
